abdomen: the body cavity between thorax and pelvis containing the digestive organs, liver, spleen, kidneys, and pancreas
abscess: a localized collection of pus walled off by inflamed tissue, caused by infection and typically requiring drainage
acetabulum: the cup-shaped socket of the pelvis that articulates with the femoral head to form the hip joint
acetylcholine: a neurotransmitter at neuromuscular junctions and in the autonomic nervous system mediating muscle contraction and parasympathetic signaling
acidosis: a pathological process producing excess acid (decreased pH or HCO3-), classified as metabolic or respiratory
acne: a chronic inflammatory disorder of pilosebaceous units producing comedones, papules, pustules, and nodules
acromegaly: a disorder of growth hormone excess in adults causing enlargement of hands, feet, and facial features
acute: of sudden onset and short duration; opposite of chronic
adenocarcinoma: a malignant epithelial tumor arising from glandular tissue (e.g., colon, lung, breast, prostate)
adenoma: a benign neoplasm of glandular epithelium, with potential for malignant transformation
adenosine: an endogenous nucleoside used IV to terminate paroxysmal SVT and as a coronary vasodilator in stress testing
adipose: connective tissue composed of fat cells (adipocytes) storing energy and providing insulation
adrenal: paired endocrine glands above each kidney producing corticosteroids, mineralocorticoids, and catecholamines
adrenaline: catecholamine (epinephrine) released from the adrenal medulla mediating fight-or-flight responses
aerobic: requiring oxygen for metabolism or growth (e.g., aerobic respiration, aerobic bacteria)
afferent: carrying signals or fluid toward a structure or central point (e.g., sensory nerves, renal afferent arterioles)
agglutination: clumping of cells (RBCs, bacteria) due to antigen-antibody binding
albumin: the major plasma protein synthesized by the liver, maintaining oncotic pressure and transporting drugs and hormones
aldosterone: a mineralocorticoid from the adrenal cortex promoting renal Na+ retention and K+ excretion
alkalosis: a pathological process producing excess base (increased pH), classified as metabolic or respiratory
allergen: a substance that triggers an IgE-mediated immune response and allergic symptoms
alopecia: loss of hair from scalp or body, classified by pattern and cause (androgenetic, areata, scarring)
alveolus: a microscopic air sac in the lungs where gas exchange between air and blood occurs
amenorrhea: absence of menstruation; primary (no menarche by 15) or secondary (cessation for ≥3 cycles)
amino acid: an organic compound with amino and carboxyl groups; the building block of proteins
amnesia: loss of memory due to brain injury, disease, or psychological trauma
amniocentesis: needle aspiration of amniotic fluid for prenatal genetic and biochemical testing
amniotic: pertaining to the membrane and fluid surrounding the fetus in utero
amylase: a digestive enzyme from pancreas and salivary glands that hydrolyzes starch to maltose
anaerobic: not requiring oxygen; growth or metabolism in the absence of O2
analgesic: a drug or agent that relieves pain without producing loss of consciousness
anaphylaxis: a severe rapid-onset systemic IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction with hypotension and airway compromise
anastomosis: a surgical or natural connection between two tubular structures (vessels, bowel)
anemia: reduced hemoglobin or RBC mass leading to impaired oxygen delivery, with multiple etiologies
anesthesia: pharmacologically induced loss of sensation (general, regional, or local) to permit procedures
aneurysm: an abnormal localized dilation of an artery wall risking rupture or thromboembolism
angina: chest pain or pressure due to myocardial ischemia, typically from coronary artery disease
angiogenesis: formation of new blood vessels from preexisting ones, important in growth, healing, and tumors
angiography: imaging of blood vessels using contrast under fluoroscopy, CT, or MRI
angioplasty: endovascular dilation of a stenosed artery, often combined with stent placement
anhedonia: inability to experience pleasure; a core symptom of major depression
anorexia: loss of appetite; also short for anorexia nervosa, a restrictive eating disorder
antibody: an immunoglobulin produced by plasma cells that binds specific antigens
anticoagulant: a drug that prevents clot formation by inhibiting coagulation factors (heparin, warfarin, DOACs)
antigen: a molecule recognized by antibodies or T-cell receptors that triggers an immune response
antihistamine: a drug blocking histamine H1 receptors, used for allergic disorders and motion sickness
antipyretic: a drug that lowers body temperature in fever (acetaminophen, NSAIDs)
aorta: the largest artery, originating from the left ventricle and supplying the systemic circulation
aphasia: acquired loss of language function from cortical injury (Broca's, Wernicke's, global, conduction)
apnea: cessation of breathing for ≥10 seconds (obstructive, central, or mixed)
apoptosis: programmed cell death without inflammation, important in development and tissue homeostasis
appendicitis: acute inflammation of the vermiform appendix presenting with periumbilical-to-RLQ pain, fever, leukocytosis
arachnoid: the middle meningeal layer between dura and pia containing CSF in the subarachnoid space
arrhythmia: an abnormal heart rhythm or rate (bradyarrhythmia, tachyarrhythmia)
arteriole: a small artery branch regulating blood flow into capillary beds and influencing systemic vascular resistance
arteriosclerosis: hardening and thickening of arterial walls, encompassing atherosclerosis and other forms
artery: a muscular vessel carrying blood from the heart to tissues (oxygenated except pulmonary arteries)
arthralgia: pain in a joint without objective signs of inflammation
arthritis: inflammation of a joint with multiple causes (osteoarthritis, RA, gout, septic arthritis)
arthroscopy: minimally invasive endoscopic surgery of a joint via small portals
ascites: pathological accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity, most commonly from cirrhosis
asphyxia: oxygen deprivation severe enough to cause unconsciousness or death
asthma: a chronic inflammatory airway disease with reversible bronchoconstriction and airway hyperresponsiveness
astrocyte: a glial cell of the CNS supporting neurons and forming the blood-brain barrier
ataxia: loss of coordination of voluntary muscle movements, often cerebellar in origin
atelectasis: collapse of alveoli or a lung segment producing impaired gas exchange
atherosclerosis: lipid and inflammatory plaque deposition in arterial walls causing stenosis and thrombosis
atrium: one of the two upper heart chambers receiving blood from the systemic or pulmonary veins
atrophy: wasting or reduction in size of tissue or organ from disuse, denervation, or disease
auscultation: clinical listening to internal sounds (heart, lungs, bowel) with a stethoscope
autoimmune: pathological immune response directed against self-antigens (e.g., SLE, RA, T1DM)
autopsy: postmortem examination to determine cause of death and disease processes
axilla: the armpit; anatomical region containing lymph nodes, vessels, and the brachial plexus
axon: the long projection of a neuron that conducts action potentials away from the cell body
bacteremia: presence of viable bacteria in the bloodstream, with or without systemic illness
basophil: a granulocyte containing histamine-rich granules involved in allergic and inflammatory responses
benign: non-cancerous; not invasive or metastatic
bilirubin: yellow pigment from heme catabolism, conjugated by the liver and excreted in bile; elevated in jaundice
biopsy: removal of tissue for histopathological examination
bradycardia: heart rate below 60 bpm in adults
bronchiole: a small distal airway lacking cartilage that leads from bronchi to alveoli
bronchitis: inflammation of the bronchial mucosa, acute (typically viral) or chronic (defining feature of COPD)
bronchus: one of the major branches of the trachea conducting air to each lung
bursitis: inflammation of a bursa (synovial sac near joints) producing pain on movement
calcaneus: the heel bone, the largest tarsal
calcification: deposition of calcium salts in tissues, normal in bone and pathologic elsewhere
calcitonin: a thyroid C-cell hormone that lowers serum calcium by inhibiting osteoclast activity
callus: thickened keratinized skin from repeated friction; or fibrous tissue forming at a healing fracture
capillary: the smallest blood vessel where exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste occurs across the endothelium
carcinoma: a malignant tumor arising from epithelial cells
cardiomegaly: enlargement of the heart, often from chronic pressure/volume overload or cardiomyopathy
cardiomyopathy: primary disease of heart muscle (dilated, hypertrophic, restrictive, arrhythmogenic)
carotid: pertaining to the major arteries of the neck supplying the head and brain
cartilage: avascular connective tissue providing structural support (hyaline, elastic, fibrocartilage)
cataract: opacification of the lens of the eye causing progressive vision loss
catheter: a flexible tube inserted into a body cavity, vessel, or duct for drainage, infusion, or measurement
cellulitis: acute bacterial infection of dermis and subcutaneous tissue with erythema, warmth, swelling, tenderness
cephalalgia: headache; pain in the head
cerebellum: the hindbrain structure coordinating movement, balance, and motor learning
cerebrospinal: pertaining to the brain and spinal cord; CSF circulates through ventricles and the subarachnoid space
cerebrum: the largest part of the brain comprising two hemispheres, responsible for higher cortical functions
cervix: the lower narrow portion of the uterus opening into the vagina
chemotherapy: use of cytotoxic drugs to treat cancer or, by older usage, infection
cholecystitis: inflammation of the gallbladder, usually due to gallstone obstruction of the cystic duct
cholelithiasis: presence of gallstones in the gallbladder
cholesterol: a sterol lipid component of cell membranes and precursor of steroid hormones; elevated levels promote ASCVD
chondrocyte: the cell type of cartilage that produces and maintains the cartilaginous matrix
chorea: brief irregular involuntary movements seen in Huntington's, Sydenham's, drug effects, or pregnancy
chromosome: a condensed DNA-protein structure carrying genetic information; humans have 46 (23 pairs)
chronic: persistent, long-lasting, or recurrent disease (typically lasting >3 months)
cirrhosis: irreversible fibrosis and nodular regeneration of the liver from chronic injury (alcohol, viral, MASH)
claudication: reproducible muscle pain on exertion relieved by rest, due to peripheral artery disease
clavicle: the collarbone, connecting sternum to scapula
clostridium: a genus of anaerobic Gram-positive spore-forming bacteria including C.difficile, C.tetani, C.botulinum, C.perfringens
coagulation: formation of a blood clot via interaction of platelets and the clotting cascade culminating in fibrin
cochlea: the spiral inner-ear structure converting sound vibrations to neural signals
colitis: inflammation of the colon (UC, Crohn's, infectious, ischemic, microscopic)
collagen: the most abundant structural protein in connective tissue, found in skin, bone, tendon, and cartilage
colonoscopy: endoscopic examination of the colon for screening and diagnosis of colonic disease
colostomy: surgical creation of an opening between the colon and the abdominal wall for fecal diversion
comorbidity: presence of one or more additional diseases co-occurring with a primary condition
concussion: a mild traumatic brain injury producing transient neurological dysfunction without structural damage on imaging
congenital: present at birth, whether genetic or acquired in utero
conjunctivitis: inflammation of the conjunctiva (viral, bacterial, allergic, chemical)
contraindication: a clinical condition that makes a particular treatment or procedure inadvisable
contusion: a bruise; soft tissue injury without skin breakage causing extravasation of blood
cornea: the transparent anterior surface of the eye providing most of its refractive power
coronary: pertaining to the arteries supplying the myocardium
corpuscle: a small free-floating body, especially a blood cell or a sensory receptor (e.g., Pacinian corpuscle)
cortex: the outer layer of an organ (cerebral, renal, adrenal)
corticosteroid: an adrenal cortex steroid hormone or synthetic analog with anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects
cortisol: the major endogenous glucocorticoid regulating metabolism, immune function, and the stress response
creatinine: a muscle metabolite cleared by the kidneys, used as a marker of renal function
crepitus: a grating, crackling, or popping sensation/sound (joints, subcutaneous emphysema, pleural)
cyanosis: bluish discoloration of skin and mucosa from increased deoxygenated hemoglobin (>5 g/dL)
cystitis: inflammation of the bladder, usually from bacterial UTI
cytokine: a small protein signaling molecule mediating immune and inflammatory responses (interleukins, interferons, TNF)
cytology: microscopic study of individual cells, often for cancer screening (Pap smear, FNA)
cytoplasm: the intracellular fluid and organelles outside the nucleus
debridement: removal of dead, damaged, or infected tissue from a wound to promote healing
defibrillation: delivery of an unsynchronized electrical shock to terminate VF or pulseless VT
dehydration: reduction in total body water, typically with hypovolemia and electrolyte disturbance
dementia: acquired progressive cognitive decline interfering with daily function (Alzheimer's, vascular, LBD, FTD)
dendrite: the branched neuronal projection that receives synaptic input
dermatitis: inflammation of the skin (atopic, contact, seborrheic, stasis)
dermatology: the medical specialty concerned with skin, hair, nails, and mucous membranes
dermis: the middle skin layer beneath the epidermis containing collagen, vessels, nerves, and adnexal structures
diabetes: a metabolic disease of chronic hyperglycemia from insulin deficiency or resistance (T1DM, T2DM, gestational)
dialysis: extracorporeal removal of waste and water from blood when kidneys fail (hemodialysis, peritoneal)
diaphoresis: profuse sweating, often from systemic illness, hypoglycemia, or autonomic activation
diaphragm: the dome-shaped muscle separating thoracic and abdominal cavities; principal muscle of inspiration
diaphysis: the shaft of a long bone between the proximal and distal epiphyses
diastole: the relaxation phase of the cardiac cycle when the ventricles fill
diplopia: double vision from misalignment of the visual axes (binocular) or ocular pathology (monocular)
diuretic: a drug that increases urine output by altering renal sodium handling (loop, thiazide, K-sparing)
diverticulitis: inflammation/infection of a colonic diverticulum, usually presenting with LLQ pain and fever
dorsal: pertaining to the back or posterior aspect of the body
duodenum: the first portion of the small intestine receiving gastric, pancreatic, and biliary secretions
dura mater: the tough outer meningeal layer covering the brain and spinal cord
dysentery: inflammatory diarrhea with blood and mucus, typically infectious (Shigella, amoebic)
dyslipidemia: abnormal blood lipid levels (high LDL/triglycerides, low HDL) increasing ASCVD risk
dysmenorrhea: painful menstruation, primary (no pelvic pathology) or secondary (e.g., endometriosis)
dyspepsia: indigestion; upper abdominal discomfort related to eating
dysphagia: difficulty swallowing, oropharyngeal or esophageal in origin
dysphasia: impaired language function, often used interchangeably with aphasia
dysplasia: abnormal cellular growth or development, often premalignant (e.g., cervical dysplasia)
dyspnea: subjective sensation of breathing discomfort or shortness of breath
dystonia: sustained or intermittent involuntary muscle contractions producing twisting postures
dystrophy: progressive degeneration of muscle or other tissue, often inherited (e.g., Duchenne)
dysuria: painful or burning urination, typically from UTI or urethritis
ecchymosis: a bruise larger than 1 cm from extravasated blood under intact skin
echocardiogram: ultrasound imaging of cardiac structure and function (transthoracic or transesophageal)
eclampsia: new-onset seizures in a pregnant or postpartum patient with preeclampsia
ectopic: located outside its normal position (e.g., ectopic pregnancy, ectopic atrial foci)
eczema: a chronic itchy inflammatory skin condition; often used synonymously with atopic dermatitis
edema: excess interstitial fluid producing tissue swelling
efferent: carrying signals or fluid away from a central structure (motor nerves, renal efferent arterioles)
ejection fraction: percentage of left ventricular blood ejected per beat (normal ≥50%)
electrocardiogram: surface recording of the heart's electrical activity through skin electrodes
electrolyte: charged ion in body fluids regulating osmolality, nerve, and muscle function (Na, K, Cl, Ca, Mg, HCO3)
embolism: obstruction of a vessel by a thrombus or other material that traveled from elsewhere
embolus: the traveling clot, fat, air, or other material that lodges and obstructs a vessel
emphysema: permanent destructive enlargement of distal airspaces with loss of elastic recoil; a form of COPD
empyema: accumulation of pus in a body cavity, typically pleural
encephalitis: inflammation of the brain parenchyma, usually viral, presenting with fever, seizures, altered mental status
encephalopathy: diffuse brain dysfunction (metabolic, toxic, hepatic, hypoxic) producing altered mental status
endarterectomy: surgical removal of atherosclerotic plaque from an artery (commonly carotid)
endocarditis: inflammation of the endocardium, especially heart valves, usually infective
endocrine: pertaining to ductless glands secreting hormones into the bloodstream
endometriosis: presence of endometrial tissue outside the uterus causing pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, and infertility
endometrium: the mucosal lining of the uterus that thickens and sheds with the menstrual cycle
endoscopy: direct visualization of internal lumens via a flexible scope (EGD, colonoscopy, bronchoscopy)
endothelium: the single-cell layer lining blood vessels, modulating tone, coagulation, and permeability
enuresis: involuntary urination, especially at night in children older than 5 years
enzyme: a protein catalyst that accelerates a specific biochemical reaction
eosinophil: a granulocyte involved in parasitic infections, allergy, and certain immune responses
epicardium: the outer layer of the heart wall (visceral pericardium)
epidermis: the outer avascular layer of the skin composed primarily of stratified squamous keratinizing epithelium
epididymis: the coiled tubule on the testis where spermatozoa mature and are stored
epidural: located outside the dura mater (epidural anesthesia, epidural hematoma)
epiglottis: the cartilaginous flap that covers the larynx during swallowing to prevent aspiration
epilepsy: a chronic CNS disorder of recurrent unprovoked seizures
epinephrine: a catecholamine secreted by the adrenal medulla; same molecule as adrenaline; used in anaphylaxis and arrest
epiphysis: the end of a long bone, separated from the shaft by the growth plate in children
epistaxis: nosebleed; anterior (Kiesselbach's plexus) or posterior
epithelium: the cellular lining of body surfaces, cavities, and tubes
erythema: redness of the skin from capillary dilation
erythrocyte: a red blood cell carrying oxygen via hemoglobin
erythropoietin: a renal hormone stimulating RBC production in the bone marrow
esophagus: the muscular tube conveying food from pharynx to stomach
estrogen: the principal female sex steroid promoting development of secondary sex characteristics and the menstrual cycle
etiology: the cause or set of causes of a disease
exocrine: pertaining to glands that secrete via ducts onto a surface or into a cavity
exophthalmos: protrusion of the eyeball from the orbit, classically in Graves' disease
extubation: removal of an endotracheal tube once a patient can breathe and protect the airway
exudate: inflammatory fluid with high protein and cellular content leaking from vessels
fascia: sheets of connective tissue investing muscles, organs, and other structures
febrile: pertaining to or having fever
femur: the thigh bone; the longest bone in the human body
fetus: the unborn human from approximately week 9 of gestation until birth
fibrillation: rapid uncoordinated contractions (atrial or ventricular) producing chaotic electrical activity
fibrin: an insoluble protein meshwork formed from fibrinogen during clot formation
fibroblast: a connective tissue cell that produces collagen and extracellular matrix
fibromyalgia: a chronic pain syndrome with widespread tenderness, fatigue, and sleep disturbance
fibrosis: excessive deposition of fibrous tissue in response to chronic injury
fissure: a narrow groove or cleft (anal fissure, lung fissure)
fistula: an abnormal communication between two epithelialized surfaces or organs
flatulence: excessive gas in the GI tract producing belching or flatus
follicle: a small spherical group of cells (hair, ovarian, lymphoid)
fontanelle: a soft membranous gap between cranial bones in infants that closes with growth
foramen: an opening or perforation in bone or membrane allowing passage of vessels or nerves
fracture: a break in the continuity of a bone (open, closed, comminuted, greenstick)
fundus: the base or deepest part of an organ (gastric fundus, ocular fundus, uterine fundus)
gallbladder: the pear-shaped organ beneath the liver that stores and concentrates bile
gangrene: tissue death from ischemia or infection (dry, wet, gas)
gastrectomy: surgical removal of part or all of the stomach
gastritis: inflammation of the gastric mucosa, often from H.pylori, NSAIDs, or alcohol
gastroenteritis: inflammation of stomach and intestines causing vomiting and diarrhea, usually viral
gingivitis: inflammation of the gums from plaque accumulation
glaucoma: a group of optic neuropathies with progressive vision loss, often associated with elevated intraocular pressure
glioblastoma: a grade IV astrocytoma; the most aggressive primary brain tumor
glomerulus: the capillary tuft within a renal corpuscle where blood is filtered to form primary urine
glucagon: an alpha-cell pancreatic hormone that raises blood glucose by promoting hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis
glucose: the principal blood sugar and primary energy substrate for cells
glycogen: the stored polymer form of glucose, mainly in liver and muscle
goiter: enlargement of the thyroid gland with or without abnormal hormonal function
gonorrhea: a sexually transmitted infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae
granulocyte: a WBC with cytoplasmic granules (neutrophil, eosinophil, basophil)
granuloma: an organized collection of macrophages and other cells responding to chronic stimulus (TB, sarcoid, foreign body)
gynecomastia: benign enlargement of male breast tissue from estrogen/androgen imbalance
halitosis: persistent bad breath, usually from oral or systemic causes
hamstring: the posterior thigh muscle group (semitendinosus, semimembranosus, biceps femoris)
hematemesis: vomiting of blood, indicating upper GI bleeding
hematocrit: the percentage of blood volume occupied by RBCs
hematoma: a localized collection of extravasated blood within tissue
hematuria: blood in urine, gross or microscopic
hemiplegia: paralysis of one side of the body, typically from contralateral CNS lesion
hemochromatosis: a disorder of iron overload damaging liver, heart, pancreas, joints, and skin
hemodialysis: extracorporeal removal of solutes and water from blood across a semipermeable membrane
hemoglobin: the iron-containing oxygen-carrying protein in RBCs
hemolysis: destruction of red blood cells with release of hemoglobin
hemophilia: an X-linked bleeding disorder from deficiency of clotting factor VIII (A) or IX (B)
hemoptysis: coughing up blood from the lower respiratory tract
hemorrhage: active bleeding, internal or external, often graded by severity
hemorrhoid: engorgement of the venous plexus around the anus, internal or external
hemostasis: the physiological process of stopping bleeding via vasoconstriction, platelet plug, and coagulation
hepatitis: inflammation of the liver from viral, autoimmune, alcoholic, drug-induced, or toxic causes
hepatomegaly: enlargement of the liver beyond its normal span
hernia: protrusion of an organ or tissue through the wall of the cavity that contains it
herpes: viral infection by HSV-1, HSV-2 (oral/genital), or VZV (chickenpox/shingles)
hippocampus: a medial temporal lobe structure essential for new declarative memory formation
hirsutism: excess male-pattern terminal hair growth in women, often from hyperandrogenism
histamine: a vasoactive amine from mast cells and basophils mediating allergy and gastric acid secretion
histology: the microscopic study of tissue architecture and cells
homeostasis: maintenance of stable internal physiological conditions despite external changes
hormone: a chemical messenger secreted by an endocrine gland and acting on distant target tissues
humerus: the bone of the upper arm
hydrocephalus: abnormal accumulation of CSF in the cerebral ventricles causing increased intracranial pressure
hyperbilirubinemia: elevated serum bilirubin causing jaundice; conjugated, unconjugated, or mixed
hypercalcemia: elevated serum calcium, commonly from primary hyperparathyroidism or malignancy
hypercapnia: elevated arterial CO2 (PaCO2 >45 mmHg), indicating ventilatory failure
hyperglycemia: elevated blood glucose; the hallmark of diabetes mellitus
hyperkalemia: elevated serum potassium risking cardiac arrhythmia and peaked T waves on ECG
hyperlipidemia: elevated blood lipid levels (cholesterol, triglycerides) increasing ASCVD risk
hyperplasia: increase in cell number leading to tissue or organ enlargement (reversible)
hypertension: persistently elevated blood pressure (≥130/80 by current ACC/AHA guidelines)
hyperthyroidism: excess thyroid hormone causing weight loss, palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor
hypertrophy: increase in cell size leading to tissue enlargement
hypocalcemia: low serum calcium causing tetany, paresthesias, and Chvostek/Trousseau signs
hypoglycemia: low blood glucose, often from insulin or sulfonylurea, producing neuroglycopenia and adrenergic symptoms
hypokalemia: low serum potassium causing weakness, arrhythmia, and U waves on ECG
hyponatremia: low serum sodium with neurological symptoms when severe; classified by tonicity and volume status
hypotension: low blood pressure with possible organ hypoperfusion
hypothalamus: a diencephalic region regulating homeostasis, autonomic, and endocrine function via the pituitary
hypothermia: core body temperature <35°C with risk of arrhythmia and metabolic disturbance
hypothyroidism: deficient thyroid hormone causing fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, bradycardia, constipation
hypovolemia: reduced circulating blood volume with risk of hypotension and shock
hypoxemia: low arterial oxygen tension (PaO2 <80 mmHg)
hypoxia: insufficient tissue oxygen delivery, may or may not coincide with hypoxemia
hysterectomy: surgical removal of the uterus, with or without cervix and adnexa
iatrogenic: caused inadvertently by medical examination or treatment
icterus: jaundice; yellow discoloration of skin and sclerae from hyperbilirubinemia
idiopathic: of unknown cause
ileum: the distal small intestine, the site of B12 and bile acid absorption
ileus: functional cessation of bowel motility without mechanical obstruction
immunoglobulin: an antibody produced by plasma cells (IgG, IgA, IgM, IgD, IgE)
infarction: tissue death from ischemia, classically myocardial, cerebral, splenic, renal, or bowel
inflammation: tissue response to injury characterized by redness, heat, swelling, pain, and loss of function
influenza: an acute respiratory illness from influenza A or B viruses, often seasonal and epidemic
inguinal: pertaining to the groin region
insomnia: difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep with daytime impairment
insulin: a beta-cell pancreatic hormone lowering blood glucose by promoting cellular glucose uptake and storage
intercostal: located between the ribs (muscles, nerves, vessels)
intracranial: located within the cranial cavity
intubation: insertion of a tube into the trachea (or other lumen) for airway protection or ventilation
ischemia: insufficient blood supply to tissue causing hypoxia and risk of infarction
jaundice: yellow discoloration of skin and sclerae from hyperbilirubinemia
jejunum: the middle portion of small intestine between duodenum and ileum, primary site of nutrient absorption
keratin: a fibrous structural protein of epidermis, hair, and nails
keratitis: inflammation of the cornea, infectious or non-infectious
ketoacidosis: metabolic acidosis from ketone accumulation, classically diabetic ketoacidosis
ketone: an acidic byproduct of fatty acid oxidation accumulating during fasting or insulin deficiency
kyphosis: excessive convex posterior curvature of the thoracic spine
labyrinth: the inner ear structures of cochlea and vestibular apparatus
laceration: a torn or jagged wound from blunt or shearing trauma
lacrimal: pertaining to tears or the tear-producing apparatus
laparoscopy: minimally invasive abdominal surgery using small ports and a video camera
laparotomy: open surgical incision of the abdominal wall to access intraperitoneal contents
laryngitis: inflammation of the larynx producing hoarseness or aphonia, often viral
larynx: the voice box; cartilaginous airway structure between pharynx and trachea housing the vocal cords
leukemia: a malignancy of hematopoietic cells with bone marrow and peripheral blood involvement (acute or chronic, myeloid or lymphoid)
leukocyte: a white blood cell of the immune system (granulocytes, lymphocytes, monocytes)
leukocytosis: elevated WBC count, typically from infection, inflammation, or malignancy
leukopenia: low WBC count from marrow suppression, sepsis, or autoimmune disease
ligament: fibrous connective tissue connecting bones at joints
lipase: a pancreatic and lingual enzyme hydrolyzing triglycerides; serum elevation indicates pancreatitis
lipoma: a benign tumor of mature adipose tissue
lordosis: excessive concave anterior curvature of the lumbar spine
lumen: the interior cavity of a tubular structure (vessel, intestine)
lumbar: pertaining to the lower back between thorax and pelvis (vertebrae L1-L5)
lupus: systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease with multi-organ involvement and ANA positivity
lymphadenopathy: abnormal enlargement of lymph nodes from infection, autoimmunity, or malignancy
lymphocyte: a WBC of adaptive immunity (B cells, T cells, NK cells)
lymphoma: a malignancy of lymphocytes (Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin)
macrophage: a tissue-resident phagocyte derived from monocytes, important in innate and adaptive immunity
malignant: cancerous; capable of invasion and metastasis
mammography: X-ray imaging of the breast for screening and diagnosis of breast cancer
mandible: the lower jaw bone
mastectomy: surgical removal of breast tissue for cancer treatment or risk reduction
mastitis: inflammation of breast tissue, often during lactation, with or without bacterial infection
maxilla: the upper jaw bone forming part of the orbit, palate, and nasal cavity
mediastinum: the central thoracic compartment between the lungs containing heart, great vessels, esophagus, trachea
medulla: the inner part of an organ (renal, adrenal); also the brainstem region controlling vital autonomic functions
melanin: the pigment produced by melanocytes giving color to skin, hair, and eyes
melanoma: an aggressive malignancy of melanocytes, often arising in skin and prone to early metastasis
melena: black tarry stool from upper GI bleeding (oxidized blood)
meninges: the three membranous coverings of the CNS (dura, arachnoid, pia)
meningitis: inflammation of the meninges, infectious (bacterial, viral, fungal) or non-infectious
menorrhagia: heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding (>80 mL or >7 days)
menstruation: cyclic shedding of the endometrium with bleeding, occurring approximately monthly during reproductive years
metabolism: the set of chemical processes that sustain life, including catabolism and anabolism
metacarpal: one of the five long bones of the palm of the hand
metastasis: spread of cancer from primary site to a distant organ
metatarsal: one of the five long bones of the forefoot between tarsals and phalanges
microbiome: the community of microorganisms inhabiting a body site (gut, skin, oral, vaginal)
migraine: a primary headache disorder of recurrent moderate-to-severe unilateral throbbing pain, often with aura, photophobia, and phonophobia
mitosis: the cellular process of dividing chromosomes equally between two daughter cells
mitral: pertaining to the bicuspid valve between the left atrium and left ventricle
monocyte: a WBC that differentiates into tissue macrophages and dendritic cells
morbidity: the state of disease or its incidence in a population
mortality: death rate or the condition of being subject to death
mucosa: a mucous membrane lining body cavities and tubes communicating with the exterior
mucus: viscous secretion of mucous glands lubricating and protecting epithelial surfaces
myalgia: muscle pain
myasthenia: muscle weakness; classically myasthenia gravis from anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies
mycosis: a fungal infection
mydriasis: pupillary dilation from sympathetic activation, drugs, or pathology
myelin: the lipid-rich sheath around axons enabling rapid saltatory conduction
myeloma: multiple myeloma; a plasma cell malignancy producing monoclonal immunoglobulin and lytic bone lesions
myocardial: pertaining to the heart muscle
myocarditis: inflammation of the heart muscle, often viral, presenting with HF, chest pain, or arrhythmia
myocardium: the middle muscular layer of the heart wall
myoma: a benign smooth muscle tumor (e.g., uterine fibroid/leiomyoma)
myopathy: a disease of muscle, hereditary or acquired (inflammatory, toxic, metabolic, endocrine)
myopia: nearsightedness; refractive error focusing images in front of the retina
narcolepsy: a chronic sleep disorder of excessive daytime sleepiness with cataplexy and REM intrusion
nausea: subjective sensation of impending vomiting
necrosis: pathological cell death from injury, with associated inflammation
neonatal: pertaining to the newborn period (first 28 days of life)
neoplasm: an abnormal new tissue growth, benign or malignant
nephrectomy: surgical removal of a kidney
nephritis: inflammation of the kidney (glomerulonephritis, interstitial nephritis)
nephrolithiasis: kidney stones; calculi within the urinary tract
nephron: the functional unit of the kidney comprising glomerulus and tubule
nephropathy: any disease of the kidney
neuralgia: pain along the distribution of a nerve
neurogenic: originating from or caused by a nerve or the nervous system
neuron: a nerve cell that transmits electrical and chemical signals
neuropathy: disease or dysfunction of peripheral nerves causing weakness, sensory loss, or pain
neutropenia: reduced absolute neutrophil count predisposing to bacterial and fungal infection
neutrophil: the most abundant WBC, central to acute innate immune response and bacterial defense
nodule: a small solid lesion ≤3 cm in skin, lung, thyroid, or other tissue
nystagmus: involuntary rhythmic eye movements, central or peripheral in origin
occlusion: blockage or closure of a vessel or lumen
olfactory: pertaining to the sense of smell
oliguria: reduced urine output (<400 mL/day or <0.5 mL/kg/h in adults)
oncology: the medical specialty of cancer diagnosis and treatment
ophthalmology: the medical specialty of the eye and visual system
optic: pertaining to the eye or vision
orchitis: inflammation of the testis, often viral (mumps) or bacterial
osmosis: movement of water across a semipermeable membrane from low to high solute concentration
osseous: pertaining to bone
ossification: the process of bone formation from cartilage (endochondral) or membrane (intramembranous)
osteoarthritis: a degenerative joint disease of cartilage loss, osteophyte formation, and pain on use
osteoblast: a bone-forming cell that synthesizes osteoid
osteoclast: a multinucleated bone-resorbing cell of monocyte lineage
osteomyelitis: infection of bone, typically bacterial, presenting with pain, fever, and elevated inflammatory markers
osteoporosis: reduced bone mass and microarchitectural deterioration with increased fracture risk (T-score ≤−2.5)
otitis: inflammation of the ear (externa, media, interna)
otosclerosis: abnormal bone growth in the middle ear causing progressive conductive hearing loss
ovary: the female gonad producing oocytes and sex hormones
oviduct: the fallopian tube; conduit from ovary to uterus where fertilization typically occurs
ovulation: release of an oocyte from the ovary, typically mid-cycle
oxytocin: a posterior pituitary hormone causing uterine contraction in labor and milk letdown in lactation
palliative: care aimed at relieving symptoms and improving quality of life rather than curing disease
pallor: paleness of skin or mucosa from anemia, vasoconstriction, or shock
palpation: physical examination by feeling with the hands
palpitation: subjective awareness of one's own heartbeat, often as fluttering, pounding, or skipping
pancreas: a retroperitoneal gland with exocrine (digestive enzymes) and endocrine (insulin, glucagon) functions
pancreatitis: inflammation of the pancreas, acute or chronic, often from gallstones or alcohol
pandemic: an epidemic of an infectious disease that has spread across continents or globally
papilledema: swelling of the optic disc due to elevated intracranial pressure
papule: a small solid raised skin lesion (<1 cm in diameter)
paralysis: loss of voluntary muscle function from neural or muscular dysfunction
paraplegia: paralysis of both legs, usually from thoracic or lumbar spinal cord injury
parasympathetic: the branch of the autonomic nervous system mediating rest-and-digest functions via vagus and sacral nerves
parathyroid: four small glands posterior to the thyroid producing parathyroid hormone (PTH) to raise serum calcium
parenchyma: the functional tissue of an organ, distinct from supportive stroma
parenteral: administered by injection or infusion (IV, IM, SC), bypassing the GI tract
paresthesia: abnormal sensation such as tingling, numbness, prickling, or burning
parietal: pertaining to the wall of a cavity (parietal pleura, parietal peritoneum, parietal lobe)
parkinsonism: a movement disorder of bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor, and postural instability
paronychia: infection or inflammation of the skin around a fingernail or toenail
parotid: the largest salivary gland, located anterior to the ear and a target of mumps
parturition: the process of childbirth
patella: the kneecap; sesamoid bone within the quadriceps tendon
pathogen: an organism capable of causing disease
pathology: the study of disease processes; also tissue diagnosis by biopsy or autopsy
pectoral: pertaining to the chest, especially the chest wall muscles (pectoralis major and minor)
pediatrics: the medical specialty caring for infants, children, and adolescents
pelvis: the bony ring connecting spine to lower limbs; also the renal pelvis collecting urine
pemphigus: an autoimmune blistering disease with intraepithelial bullae from anti-desmoglein antibodies
peptic: pertaining to digestion or to peptic ulcer disease
perforation: a hole or tear through a hollow organ (bowel, gastric ulcer, eardrum)
pericarditis: inflammation of the pericardium with pleuritic chest pain, friction rub, and diffuse ST elevations
pericardium: the fibrous and serous sac surrounding the heart
perineum: the region between anus and external genitalia
periosteum: the fibrous membrane covering bones, important for nutrition, attachment, and repair
peripheral: located away from the center, especially of the nervous or vascular systems
peristalsis: coordinated rhythmic muscle contractions propelling contents through hollow organs
peritoneum: the serous membrane lining the abdominal cavity and covering most viscera
peritonitis: inflammation of the peritoneum, often from perforation, with rigidity and rebound tenderness
petechiae: pinpoint hemorrhages in skin or mucosa from capillary damage or thrombocytopenia
phagocytosis: cellular engulfment of particles or microbes by macrophages or neutrophils
phalanges: the bones of the fingers and toes
pharmacokinetics: the study of drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME)
pharyngitis: inflammation of the pharynx, usually viral but may be streptococcal
pharynx: the throat; muscular tube extending from skull base to esophagus and larynx
phlebitis: inflammation of a vein, often with thrombus formation
phlebotomy: therapeutic or diagnostic withdrawal of blood from a vein
phototherapy: treatment with light, used for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and skin diseases such as psoriasis
pituitary: the master endocrine gland at the skull base secreting trophic hormones controlling other glands
placenta: the fetomaternal organ providing nutrient and gas exchange and hormone production during pregnancy
plantar: pertaining to the sole of the foot
plasma: the acellular liquid component of blood containing proteins, electrolytes, hormones, and clotting factors
platelet: a small anucleate cell fragment from megakaryocytes essential for hemostasis
pleura: the serous membrane lining the lungs (visceral) and thoracic cavity (parietal)
pleurisy: pleural inflammation causing sharp pleuritic chest pain worsened by inspiration
plexus: a network of nerves or vessels (brachial plexus, choroid plexus)
pneumonia: infection of lung parenchyma with consolidation, presenting with fever, cough, sputum, and dyspnea
pneumothorax: air in the pleural space causing partial or complete lung collapse
polycythemia: increased RBC mass, primary (polycythemia vera) or secondary (chronic hypoxia, EPO use)
polydipsia: excessive thirst, classically in diabetes mellitus and diabetes insipidus
polyp: a protruding growth from a mucous membrane (colonic, nasal, uterine, gastric)
polyphagia: excessive hunger, classically in diabetes mellitus
polyuria: excessive urine output (>3 L/day in adults)
posterior: located toward the back of the body
postpartum: the period following childbirth (typically the first 6 weeks)
preeclampsia: pregnancy-associated hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction
presbyopia: age-related loss of accommodation causing difficulty with near vision
priapism: prolonged painful erection unrelated to sexual stimulation, requiring emergent care to prevent ischemia
proctitis: inflammation of the rectum (UC, infectious, radiation)
progesterone: the principal corpus luteum and placental steroid maintaining pregnancy and modulating the endometrium
prognosis: the predicted course or outcome of a disease
prolapse: falling or sliding of an organ from its normal position (uterine, rectal, mitral valve)
prophylaxis: preventive treatment to avoid disease or its complications
prostatitis: inflammation of the prostate, acute or chronic, bacterial or non-bacterial
proteinuria: excess protein in urine (>150 mg/day), often indicating glomerular disease
prothrombin: factor II of the coagulation cascade; PT/INR measures the extrinsic pathway
pruritus: itching, with many local and systemic causes
psoriasis: a chronic immune-mediated skin disease of well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale
psychosis: a mental state with loss of contact with reality (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thought)
ptosis: drooping of the upper eyelid from levator weakness or oculomotor (CN III) dysfunction
pulmonary: pertaining to the lungs
purpura: purple skin discoloration (>3 mm) from bleeding into skin or mucous membranes
purulent: containing or producing pus
pustule: a small pus-filled skin lesion
pyelonephritis: infection of the renal parenchyma and pelvis with fever, flank pain, and pyuria
pyloric: pertaining to the pylorus, the gastric outlet to the duodenum
pyogenic: producing pus
pyrexia: fever; elevated body temperature
quadriplegia: paralysis of all four limbs, typically from cervical spinal cord injury
rachitis: rickets; childhood vitamin D deficiency causing defective mineralization and skeletal deformity
radiculopathy: dysfunction of a nerve root from compression or inflammation, with dermatomal symptoms
radiography: imaging using X-rays to visualize internal structures
radiology: the medical specialty using imaging for diagnosis and image-guided intervention
rales: crackling lung sounds from fluid in alveoli (synonymous with crackles)
remission: reduction or absence of disease signs and symptoms, partial or complete
renal: pertaining to the kidney
respiration: gas exchange between organism and environment, including ventilation and cellular metabolism
reticulocyte: an immature RBC; elevated count indicates appropriate marrow response to anemia
retina: the light-sensitive neural layer of the eye containing rods and cones
retinopathy: non-inflammatory damage to the retina, classically diabetic or hypertensive
rhabdomyolysis: breakdown of skeletal muscle releasing myoglobin and CK, risking AKI and electrolyte disturbance
rhinitis: inflammation of nasal mucosa (allergic, viral, vasomotor)
rhinorrhea: runny nose; nasal discharge
rhonchi: low-pitched continuous lung sounds from secretions in larger airways
rickets: childhood vitamin D deficiency causing defective bone mineralization and skeletal deformity
rigor: a bout of shivering associated with fever; or rigidity of muscle (rigor mortis)
rosacea: a chronic facial skin condition with central erythema, telangiectasias, and papulopustules
rubella: German measles; mild viral exanthem with severe congenital infection risk
rubor: redness, one of the cardinal signs of inflammation (along with calor, tumor, dolor)
saliva: oral secretion containing amylase, antimicrobials, and lubricants
salpingitis: inflammation of the fallopian tube, often part of pelvic inflammatory disease
sarcoidosis: a multisystem granulomatous disease of unknown etiology, commonly involving lungs and lymph nodes
sarcoma: a malignancy of mesenchymal origin (bone, muscle, fat, fibrous tissue)
scapula: the shoulder blade, articulating with humerus and clavicle
schizophrenia: a chronic psychotic disorder with delusions, hallucinations, disorganization, and negative symptoms
sciatica: pain radiating along the sciatic nerve from lumbosacral nerve root irritation
sclera: the white fibrous outer coat of the eyeball
scleroderma: a connective tissue disease with skin and visceral fibrosis (limited or diffuse systemic sclerosis)
scoliosis: lateral curvature of the spine greater than 10 degrees
scotoma: a blind spot or area of reduced vision within the visual field
sebaceous: pertaining to oil-secreting glands of the skin
sebum: the oily lipid-rich secretion of sebaceous glands
seizure: abnormal hypersynchronous neuronal discharge with motor, sensory, autonomic, or cognitive manifestations
sepsis: life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated host response to infection
septicemia: bacteria in blood with systemic illness; older term largely replaced by bacteremia and sepsis
septum: a dividing wall between two cavities or structures (nasal, atrial, ventricular)
serotonin: a monoamine neurotransmitter (5-HT) involved in mood, GI motility, and platelet aggregation
serum: the cell-free fluid remaining after blood clots; lacks fibrinogen
shingles: reactivation of varicella-zoster virus producing dermatomal vesicular rash and postherpetic neuralgia
sialolithiasis: salivary gland stones causing painful gland swelling, especially with eating
sigmoidoscopy: endoscopic examination of the sigmoid colon and rectum
sinusitis: inflammation of the paranasal sinuses, viral or bacterial
somatic: pertaining to the body (vs psyche), or to the body wall (vs viscera)
spasm: sudden involuntary muscle contraction
sphincter: a circular muscle that closes a body opening or passageway when contracted
spirometry: pulmonary function test measuring airflow volumes and rates (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC)
splenectomy: surgical removal of the spleen
splenomegaly: enlargement of the spleen beyond its normal size
spondylitis: inflammation of the spinal vertebrae (e.g., ankylosing spondylitis)
sputum: material expectorated from the lower respiratory tract
stenosis: abnormal narrowing of a passageway (vascular, valvular, GI, spinal)
sternum: the breastbone in the anterior thorax, comprising manubrium, body, and xiphoid
steroid: a class of lipid molecules with a four-ring structure, including hormones and corticosteroids
stoma: a surgically created opening on the body surface (colostomy, ileostomy, tracheostomy)
stomatitis: inflammation of the oral mucosa
strabismus: misalignment of the eyes from extraocular muscle imbalance
stridor: a high-pitched inspiratory sound from upper airway obstruction
subarachnoid: located between the arachnoid and pia mater, where CSF flows
subcutaneous: located beneath the skin in the hypodermis
subdural: located beneath the dura mater (above the arachnoid)
sublingual: beneath the tongue; a route of drug administration with rapid absorption
supraventricular: originating above the ventricles, especially in the atria or AV node
syncope: transient loss of consciousness from global cerebral hypoperfusion with spontaneous recovery
syndrome: a characteristic constellation of signs and symptoms occurring together
synovial: pertaining to the membrane lining joints and the lubricating fluid it produces
syphilis: a sexually transmitted infection caused by Treponema pallidum, with primary, secondary, latent, and tertiary stages
systole: the contraction phase of the cardiac cycle when ventricles eject blood
tachycardia: heart rate >100 bpm in adults
tachypnea: rapid breathing rate (>20 breaths/min in adults)
talus: the ankle bone articulating with tibia and fibula
tendinitis: inflammation of a tendon from overuse or injury
tendon: fibrous connective tissue connecting muscle to bone
tenesmus: painful, ineffective urge to defecate or urinate
teratogenic: capable of causing fetal malformation when present during pregnancy
testosterone: the principal male androgen produced by Leydig cells, mediating male secondary sex characteristics
tetanus: a wound infection by Clostridium tetani producing tetanospasmin and severe muscle spasm (lockjaw)
thalamus: a diencephalic relay center processing sensory and motor signals to the cortex
thoracentesis: needle drainage of pleural fluid for diagnosis or therapy
thorax: the chest cavity between neck and diaphragm
thrombocyte: a platelet, essential for hemostasis
thrombocytopenia: low platelet count predisposing to bleeding
thromboembolism: a detached thrombus traveling and lodging at a distant site (DVT/PE most common)
thrombolysis: pharmacologic dissolution of a thrombus using fibrinolytics (alteplase, tenecteplase)
thrombosis: formation of a blood clot within a vessel
thrombus: a clot adherent to the vessel wall composed of platelets, fibrin, and entrapped cells
thymus: a mediastinal lymphoid organ where T cells mature, prominent in childhood and involutes with age
thyroid: a neck endocrine gland producing T4, T3, and calcitonin
thyroiditis: inflammation of the thyroid (Hashimoto's, subacute, postpartum, drug-induced)
thyroxine: T4; the principal thyroid hormone, converted peripherally to active T3
tibia: the shin bone, the larger weight-bearing bone of the lower leg
tinnitus: perception of sound (ringing, buzzing) without external source
tonsillitis: inflammation of the palatine tonsils, viral or streptococcal
topical: applied to a body surface (skin, mucosa)
torticollis: wry neck; abnormal head position from cervical muscle dysfunction or spasm
toxemia: generalized illness from circulating toxins; older term for preeclampsia
trachea: the windpipe; cartilaginous airway from larynx to carina
tracheostomy: surgical opening of the trachea for long-term airway access
trauma: physical injury caused by external force
tremor: involuntary rhythmic oscillation of a body part (resting, postural, intention, action)
tricuspid: pertaining to the three-cusp valve between right atrium and right ventricle
trigeminal: pertaining to the fifth cranial nerve providing facial sensation and innervating muscles of mastication
triglyceride: a storage lipid of glycerol with three fatty acids; elevated levels in dyslipidemia
trochanter: a bony prominence on the proximal femur (greater and lesser) for muscle attachment
tuberculosis: infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, primarily pulmonary but with extrapulmonary forms
tumor: an abnormal mass of tissue, benign or malignant; also one of the cardinal signs of inflammation (swelling)
tympanic: pertaining to the eardrum or middle ear
ulcer: a break in skin or mucosa with loss of surface tissue (peptic, venous, arterial, pressure, neuropathic)
ulcerative: characterized by ulceration (e.g., ulcerative colitis)
ultrasound: imaging using high-frequency sound waves; non-ionizing modality
umbilical: pertaining to the navel or umbilical cord
uremia: a clinical syndrome of advanced renal failure with toxin accumulation and multisystem effects
ureter: the muscular tube conveying urine from kidney to bladder
urethra: the tube conveying urine from bladder to exterior; longer in males and includes prostatic, membranous, spongy parts
urethritis: inflammation of the urethra, often from STI (gonorrhea, chlamydia)
urinalysis: laboratory analysis of urine for diagnostic purposes
urology: the surgical specialty of urinary tract and male reproductive system
urticaria: hives; pruritic erythematous wheals from histamine release in the dermis
uterus: the female reproductive organ where a fetus develops
uveitis: inflammation of the uveal tract (iris, ciliary body, choroid)
uvula: the conical fleshy projection from the soft palate
vaccine: a biological preparation inducing acquired adaptive immunity to a specific pathogen
vagina: the muscular canal from the cervix to the external genitalia
vagus: the tenth cranial nerve providing parasympathetic supply to thoracoabdominal organs and motor to larynx and pharynx
varicella: chickenpox; primary infection by varicella-zoster virus producing pruritic vesicular rash
varicose: pertaining to abnormally dilated tortuous veins, typically in the legs
vasculitis: inflammation of blood vessels, primary or secondary, with multiorgan effects
vasoconstriction: narrowing of a vessel's lumen by smooth muscle contraction, raising vascular resistance
vasodilation: widening of a vessel's lumen by smooth muscle relaxation, lowering vascular resistance
vasopressin: antidiuretic hormone (ADH) from the posterior pituitary, also a vasoconstrictor at higher concentrations
vein: a vessel returning blood to the heart, typically lower-pressure than arteries and equipped with valves
venipuncture: insertion of a needle into a vein for blood draw or IV access
ventilation: movement of air in and out of the lungs
ventral: pertaining to the front or anterior of the body (synonymous with anterior in humans)
ventricle: a chamber of the heart that pumps blood, or a fluid-filled cavity in the brain containing CSF
venule: a small vein receiving blood from capillaries
vertebra: one of 33 bones forming the spinal column (7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral fused, 4 coccygeal fused)
vertigo: sensation of spinning or motion, central or peripheral in origin
vesicle: a small fluid-filled blister; or a small intracellular membrane-bound transport sac
viscera: the internal organs, especially of the abdomen and thorax
vitiligo: an autoimmune skin depigmentation from melanocyte destruction
vitreous: the transparent gel filling the posterior eye between lens and retina
volvulus: twisting of a portion of bowel around its mesentery causing obstruction and possible ischemia
vulva: the external female genitalia, including labia, clitoris, and vestibule
wheal: a raised pruritic skin lesion from dermal edema, characteristic of urticaria
wheeze: a high-pitched musical lung sound from narrowed airways, classic in asthma
xanthoma: a skin deposit of cholesterol-laden macrophages, associated with hyperlipidemia
xerosis: abnormal dryness of skin or mucous membranes
xerostomia: dry mouth from reduced salivary flow, often from medications, radiation, or Sjögren's syndrome
zoonosis: an infectious disease transmissible from animals to humans
zygote: the diploid cell formed at fertilization, the earliest developmental stage of an organism
